_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER mode presets: Magellan Clay/Megacam (f/5 Cassegrain, direct) and Magellan Baade/FourStar (f/11 Gregorian Nasmyth east, reimaged with a cold pupil)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/magellan.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/imaging/widefield.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; per instrument: title, preset (machine-readable summary of the explorer inputs), recommended_preset (prose), params, performance (validation targets), not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/megacam_magellan/ or rawdata/imaging/fourstar/, or an existing file already used by reimagers.json (keys LCOT, CS98N9, LCOUM, M18 reused, same files). derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). 'NOT FOUND' / 'NOT PUBLISHED' marks a gap; no value is filled from memory. Note: rawdata/imaging/megacam/ holds CFHT MegaCam (a different instrument); Magellan Megacam sources are in rawdata/imaging/megacam_magellan/.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, division slash, tilde operator, multiplication sign (-> x), degree sign, micro sign and the ADS mojibake prefix 'Â' normalised; whitespace collapsed (a quote also passes with all whitespace removed and/or with hyphenated line breaks joined, which covers PDF line breaks and the run-together words of the M15 text layer); ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.quote_check: Every quote (and every alternative's quote) was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text: pdftotext -layout and -raw for PDFs; tag-stripped, unescaped text and raw source for HTML; raw and decoded text for the ADS JSON record.
_meta.frames: Megacam: rows are the horizontal rows of the M15 Fig. 3 photograph of the focal plane (9 rows of 4 chips); MCM's 'rows' are the four 9-chip columns. FourStar: 2 x 2 (FSH Fig. 1). x = along a row, y = across rows; gaps are between pixel areas.

megacam_clay.title: Magellan II (Clay) 6.5 m f/5 Cassegrain / Megacam (direct imager behind a 4-element fused-silica corrector; 36 CCDs)

preset.eps_note: 1.8 m f/5 secondary / 6.5 m (M15) = 0.277; the M2 baffle size is not published; the 29 m^2 area M15 uses for throughput implies 0.355
preset.telescope_type: Cassegrain (paraboloid f/1.25 primary + convex hyperbolic f/5 secondary), Clay f/5 Cassegrain port, no Nasmyth fold; 4-element fused-silica corrector (3 lenses just behind the M1 vertex + 48 mm field-flattener = dewar window); no ADC
preset.filters: two 5-slot filter wheels + shutter in the topbox, converging beam between the third corrector lens and the field-flattener window; filters ~300 mm square
preset.chip_long_axis: along the rows (M15 Fig. 3 orientation: 9 rows of 4 chips, each chip 4608 px along the row, 2048 px across)
preset.gap_x_note: gaps between chips 1|2, 2|3, 3|4 of every row: 31" (large), 6", 31" -- DERIVED mm = arcsec x 0.169 mm/arcsec

megacam_clay.recommended_preset: D = 6.5 m (paraboloid primary, f/1.25 per LCOT), eps = 0.28 (1.8 m f/5 secondary / 6.5 m, M15; the cylindrical M2 baffle may enlarge it -- the 29 m^2 throughput area of M15 implies 0.355; 1.7 m for the MMT secondary in F04 gives 0.26), F = 5.36 = f_eff / D DERIVED (nominal 'f/5'), f_eff = 34,859 mm DERIVED from the published plate scale 0.169 mm/arcsec. Telescope focus: CASSEGRAIN on Clay (convex hyperbolic secondary, focus behind the primary vertex, instrument on the Cassegrain rotator; 'f/5 CASS focus', LCO) -- no tertiary, no Nasmyth fold. Direct imager: 4-element fused-silica corrector (three lenses just behind the M1 vertex, largest 0.83 m, + a 48 mm field-flattener that is the dewar window); no ADC; two 5-slot filter wheels and the shutter in the topbox, in the converging beam just ahead of the dewar window (filters ~300 mm square). Corrected field: 35' diameter flat focal plane (M06, MMT; correctors identical). Detector: 36 e2v CCD42-90, 2048 x 4608 px, 13.5 um. Rows (top to bottom in the M15 Fig. 3 photo): 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4 (a regular 9 x 4 grid), long axis (4608 px) along the rows. Gaps: 6" (1.01 mm, 75 px DERIVED) between all neighbours, except 31" (5.24 mm, 388 px DERIVED) between chips 1|2 and 3|4 of every row; between rows 6". Two guide CCDs outside the array. Validate: 0.08"/px (0.0799 DERIVED; usually binned to 0.16"), 25' x 25' (gap-inclusive; 24' x 24' of active pixels), 340 Mpix (339,738,624).

not_found: A Clay-specific f/5 secondary diameter or central-obscuration value: M15 gives a 1.8 m secondary for both telescopes, F04 a 1.7 m secondary for the MMT; the Clay f/5 paper (Szentgyorgyi et al. 2012, SPIE 8446) is not obtainable (abstract only, S12C). The M2 baffle diameter is not published.
A published f/5 effective focal length or exact focal ratio: only the system plate scale 0.169 mm/arcsec (M15, MCM) -> f/5.36 DERIVED.
Corrected-field size measured for the Clay f/5: the 35' flat focal plane (M06) and the 0.5 deg imaging field (F04) are MMT statements; M15 says the two correctors are identical.
Chip gaps in mm: only the on-sky 6" / 31" values (mm DERIVED with the plate scale).
conflicts: Field: 25' x 25' (M15, M06, MCM table, F04) vs 24' x 24' (MCM introduction, LCO pages) vs 0.4 deg on a side (S12C). The 24' value matches the active pixels (24.54' DERIVED), the 25' value the gap-inclusive envelope (25.7' x 25.3' DERIVED).
Gap units: M15 Sec. 1.1 and Table 1 print 6′ / 31′ (arcmin) -- a misprint; M15 Fig. 3 (caption and image) and MCM give 6" / 31" (arcsec).
Secondary diameter: 1.8 m (M15, both MMT and Clay) vs 1.7 m (F04, MMT).
Central obscuration: 0.277 (1.8 m secondary) vs 0.262 (1.7 m) vs 0.355 (DERIVED from the 29 m^2 throughput area, M15 Sec. 8.1).
Focal ratio: nominal 'f/5' vs 5.36 from the plate scale (DERIVED).
Single-CCD field: 160" x 360" published (M15, MCM) vs 163.6" x 368.1" from 2048 x 4608 px at 0.0799"/px (DERIVED).
notes: Explorer mapping: Cassegrain (no Nasmyth flat), direct imager. 9 rows of 4 chips (regular grid, rows aligned), each chip 4608 px along the row and 2048 px across; gaps along every row = 5.24, 1.01, 5.24 mm (31", 6", 31"), between rows 1.01 mm (6"). If the explorer takes one gap_x per preset, it cannot reproduce the 31/6/31 pattern; a uniform 6" gap underestimates the row length by 2 x 25" (50").
With D = 6.5 m and F = 5.363 (f_eff = 34,859 mm) the explorer reproduces 0.0799"/px at 13.5 um; with F = 5 it would give 0.0857"/px.
Megacam was recommissioned on Clay in October 2009 and used in routine operation since 2010 (M15); LCO's legacy instrument list now says 'The instrument is no longer offered' (LCOMI).
Megacam is normally read out binned 2 x 2 (0.16"/px; M15 Sec. 3.1). Two guide CCDs (same type) sit above and below the science array (M15 Fig. 3; MCM: 'centered about 20 arcmin off axis').

fourstar_baade.title: Magellan I (Baade) 6.5 m f/11 Gregorian Nasmyth (east platform) / FourStar (near-IR reimager with a cold pupil: field-lens doublet + 4-lens camera + field flattener; 2 x 2 HAWAII-2RG)

preset.eps_note: measured for Magellan Clay f/11 (twin of Baade), 'defined by the secondary baffle' (M18); L26 confirms it is a diameter ratio
preset.focus: Nasmyth East platform of Baade (NASE): f/11 Gregorian (concave secondary beyond prime focus) + flat tertiary; not a folded port
preset.f_col_note: equivalent ideal collimator = F_tel x W; the real 'collimator' is the L1/L2 fused-silica field-lens doublet (vacuum window, 210 mm behind the telescope focus) that images the primary onto the cold stop
preset.cold_stop: at the 130 mm pupil image 27 mm in front of L3 (200 K): iris (outer edge, closed to a fixed opening for Ks; default 'Closed' for all filters since 2018-04-09) + spider-mounted central disk for the secondary
preset.filters: two 6-position wheels (5 filters + open each), 94 mm square filters, near the focal plane in the f/3.6 beam, just ahead of the per-band L7 field flattener (77 K)
preset.gap_note: manual '~2 mm or ~18 arcsec'; alternatives 19" (~2.15 mm) and 150 px = 2.70 mm (P13 Table 1)

fourstar_baade.recommended_preset: D = 6.5 m, eps = 0.29 (Clay f/11 value, 'defined by the secondary baffle', M18; a diameter ratio per L26; no Baade-specific value), F_tel = 11.0 (f/11; 71,526.4 mm design, CS98N9; 2.88"/mm, FSCDR/P13), telescope focus: GREGORIAN with NASMYTH focus -- the f/11 concave Gregorian secondary (FSCDR) and the flat tertiary (documented for the Baade f/11 Nasmyth feed, LCOUM) send the beam to the EAST Nasmyth platform of Baade (P13 'East Nasmyth focus'; FSQF; LCO 'Baade NASE platform'), not a folded port; primary f/1.25 (drawing only). No telescope corrector/ADC is mentioned for FourStar. REIMAGED: L1/L2 fused-silica field-lens doublet (L1 = 381 mm vacuum window, 210 mm behind the telescope focus) forms a 130 mm pupil image 27 mm in front of L3, where the 200 K cold stop sits (iris + central disk); L3-L6 camera + per-band L7 flattener give f/3.6. Ideal-model equivalents: W = 130 mm (published), f_col = F_tel x W = 1430 mm DERIVED, f_cam = 3.6 x 130 = 468 mm DERIVED (467 mm from the as-built 0.159"/px), effective f/3.6 (published; 3.59 DERIVED; magnification 0.33). Filters: two 6-position wheels with 94 mm square filters near the focal plane (converging beam), just ahead of L7. Detector: 4 HAWAII-2RG, 2048 x 2048 (2040 x 2040 active), 18 um, rows 2, 2 (2 x 2, aligned), gaps 2.0 mm (~111 px, ~18"; FSMAN) in x and y -- published alternatives 19" and 150 px = 24". Field: 10.8' x 10.8' (FourStar corner at 160 mm = 7.7' radius in the f/11 focal plane; f/11 design field 30'). Validate: 0.159"/px, 10.8' x 10.8', 4096 x 4096 = 16.8 Mpix.

not_found: Collimator and camera focal lengths as such: FourStar has no collimated space (field-lens doublet + camera); published are the 130 mm pupil image, f/11 -> f/3.6 and 'magnification = 0.33'. f_col = 1430 mm and f_cam = 468 mm are DERIVED equivalents for the explorer's ideal model.
Cold-stop dimensions: the Ks iris opening and the central-disk diameter (P13 Sec. 7.3 gives neither).
A Baade-specific central obscuration (only the Clay f/11 value, 29%, M18/L26).
Separate x and y gaps, and which source is right among 2 mm / 18" (FSMAN), 19" (FSQF, FSH, FSOBS) and 150 px = 24" (P13 Table 1).

Whether any telescope corrector/ADC sits in the FourStar beam: none is mentioned in the FourStar documents (P13 Sec. 8.1 describes the bare f/11 field as curved and aberrated, corrected by FourStar's own optics).
conflicts: Gap between arrays: ~2 mm / ~18" (FSMAN) vs ~19" (FSQF, FSH, FSOBS) vs 150 px = 24" (P13 Table 1) vs ~1.8-1.9 mm implied by the ZEMAX footprint radii (P13 Fig. 4, DERIVED).
Field: 10.8' x 10.8' (P13, FSQF, FSMAN, FSH, FSOPT) vs 10.9' x 10.9' (P08, FSHOME) vs 11' x 11' (FSCDR).
Telescope scale: 71,526.4 mm / 346.77 um per arcsec (CS98N9) vs 2.88"/mm = 71,620 mm and 347 um/" = 71,574 mm (FSCDR, rounded).
Effective focal ratio: f/3.6 published vs f/3.59 from 0.159"/px (DERIVED); pixel scale 0.159 (most) vs 0.16 (FSOPT, FSCDR slides).
notes: Explorer mapping: Gregorian telescope with a Nasmyth flat (Baade east platform), REIMAGED imager with W = 130 mm, f_col = 1430 mm (= 11 x 130), f_cam = 468 mm (= 3.6 x 130), effective f/3.6; cold stop at the pupil; filters near the detector (converging beam). 2 x 2 square arrays of 2048 px at 18 um with 2.0 mm gaps; the telescope pointing centre falls in the central cross of the gaps (FSOBS).
With D = 6.5 m, F_tel = 11.004 (71,526.4 mm), f_cam/f_col = 468/1430 the explorer gives 0.1586"/px (published 0.159; 0.3% low). f_cam = 467 mm would reproduce 0.159 exactly.

The real optics are a field-lens reimager (PANIC-like; FSCDR): L1/L2 near the telescope focus image the primary mirror onto the cold stop (P13 Fig. 18: 'The Ks image of the primary mirror is at the axial position of the stop'), and L3-L6 + L7 form the f/3.6 image. The ideal collimator/camera pair is an equivalent with the same pupil size and magnification, not the as-built layout.
FourStar was shipped to LCO in August 2010, first light December 2010 (P13 Sec. 1).
